rationale: D2 of the growth-clock spec for inverse flames, data-informed (not zero-shot): D1 plus one law, as a scenario for a committee release. Ordered by the total mass flow through the burner, the lean train flames split cleanly: every flame up to 10.5 mg/s went out in 3-18 s, and every established flame at 17 mg/s and above was still burning at a script stop (one at 50 % oxygen, three air-injected). D1 called the 50 % one wrongly with 0.97 and explained the air-injected ones by a rule of their own. The law added here lengthens the early quench clock above a total burner flow of 12 mg/s. Whether it carries to other fuels, leaner ambients and higher pressure is not known from train: the committee release weighs this scenario against D1. Every number typed by the author; no fit, no search; no validation outcome was read, the validation conditions were.
